headline_marked: [[Araujo's late equaliser secures 1-1 draw]] for Uruguay against Saudi Arabia
headline: Araujo's late equaliser secures 1-1 draw for Uruguay against Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi Arabia, who famously beat Argentina in 2022, were on course for another World Cup upset until Maxi Araujo scored 10 minutes from time.
details: Maxi Araujo scored a late equaliser to salvage a 1-1 draw for Uruguay in their World Cup opener against Saudi Arabia on Monday. This result prevented another stunning upset in Group H, following Spain's earlier goalless draw with Cape Verde.

The Saudis had famously beaten Argentina 2-1 in their 2022 tournament opener and looked set for a repeat upset. Abdulelah Alamri's 41st-minute strike put them ahead, holding the lead until Araujo's intervention.

The Green Falcons ultimately had goalkeeper Mohammed Alowais to thank for their crucial point. This draw will give them confidence for progressing to the knockout stage, a feat they haven't achieved since 1994.
Uruguay, two-time World Cup winners, started the match with the swagger of favourites. In the fifth minute, left winger Araujo angled a shot at goal that Alowais parried away, signaling early intent.

Despite their strong start, Uruguay lacked accuracy going forward and often appeared casual at the back. A Federico Vinas diving header on the half-hour mark was also pushed away by Alowais, highlighting their struggle to convert chances.

Saudi Arabia's attack sparked into life in the 36th minute when Moteb Alharbi skipped through midfield. Alamri then had a shot well saved by Fernando Muslera two minutes later, but the Saudi pressure was building.
Mohamed Kanno got on the end of a Musab Aljuwayr corner, and although Muslera managed to save his powerful header, Alamri was on hand to tap the ball into the net, giving Saudi Arabia the lead.

Uruguay's gameplan looked more coherent after two halftime changes, with players getting down the flank to put crosses into the box. This led to a string of headers for Alowais to deal with, increasing the pressure on the Saudi goal.

Defensive midfielder Manuel Ugarte came within inches of an equaliser in the 60th minute, beating the Saudi keeper only for his drilled shot to bounce off the far post, denying Uruguay a crucial goal.

Vinas had been Uruguay's best aerial threat throughout the game, and it was no surprise that the breakthrough came from one of his headers 10 minutes from fulltime. Alowais again denied the target man, but the ball fell straight to Araujo, who controlled it well and clipped it into the net at the near post.

Uruguay poured forward looking for a winner in a frenetic finish, with Federico Valverde and Jose Maria Gimenez coming closest. Their rasping shots from either side of the box were well pushed past the post by Alowais, securing the draw for Saudi Arabia.

headline_marked: 10,500 Yaba pills and 5.8m BDT seized: [[2 drug traffickers arrested in Tongi]]
headline: 10,500 Yaba pills and 5.8m BDT seized: 2 drug traffickers arrested in Tongi
summary: Police apprehended two suspects in Tongi, recovering a significant cache of narcotics and a large sum of cash during the operation.
details: Police have arrested two drug traffickers in Tongi after seizing 10,500 Yaba pills and 5.8 million BDT in cash.
The operation targeted the suspects as part of an ongoing crackdown on narcotics trafficking in the region.
The seized cash is believed to be proceeds from illegal drug sales.
Authorities are continuing their investigation to uncover more links to the drug distribution network.
caption:
10,500 Yaba pills and 5.8 million BDT seized in a single operation. Two traffickers are now in custody.
